title: The logarithmic integral and the Rogers dilogarithm
notes: The notes write \(\int_{1-x}^{x}\{\log|t|/(1-t)+\log|1-t|/t\}\,dt\), saying it cannot be evaluated in elementary functions.
statement: For \(0<x<1\), set \(L(x)=\operatorname{Li}_2(x)+\tfrac12\log x\log(1-x)\). Then the displayed integral equals \(-2[L(x)-L(1-x)]\). This is a dilogarithmic antiderivative, not an assertion that every individual special value is non-elementary.
reconstruction: The domain and the explicit identification with the real Rogers dilogarithm are editorial; the notebook gives only the integral.
fate: This is classical dilogarithm calculus, documented with the derivative and reflection formula in \citet[Chapter II, \S1.A, pp.~23--24]{zagier2007dilogarithm}. The modern reference does not date the formula to 2007.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: The sign of the Basel integral
notes: The scan explicitly has \(\int_0^1\log|1-t|\,dt/t=+\pi^2/6\), followed by a positive power-series sum.

title: Periodic Hill operator and bounded Bloch solutions
notes: \(-y^{\prime\prime}+u(x)y=Ey\); the written periodicity is \(u(x+T)=u(y)\). The spectrum is described as the energies having bounded eigenfunctions.
statement: For real \(T\)-periodic \(u\in C^\infty(\mathbb R)\), let \(L=-d^2/dx^2+u\) on \(L^2(\mathbb R)\), domain \(H^2\). Its spectrum consists precisely of real energies with a nonzero bounded solution of \(Ly=Ey\). These are generalized eigenfunctions, generally not \(L^2(\mathbb R)\) eigenvectors.

fate: Classical Floquet theory, recapitulated in \citet[Chapter 2, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}; compare earlier occurrence 1973-326.2 and 1973-326.8.

title: Characterizing finite-gap potentials by stationary KdV
notes: \ru{Проблема Новикова: когда есть конечн. число запрещ. зон?} The answer is written as a nonlinear ordinary differential equation \(K(u,u^{\prime},\ldots,u^{(2N+1)})=0\) from the KdV hierarchy.
statement: A real smooth periodic potential has finitely many open bounded spectral gaps if and only if it is stationary for a nontrivial finite real linear combination of the KdV hierarchy flows (equivalently, its Schr\"odinger operator commutes with an odd-order scalar differential operator). The least nondegenerate order corresponds to the number of open gaps; a higher stationary equation need not have all its gaps open.
reconstruction: The phrase KdV equations is interpreted as stationary finite linear combinations, not the evolutionary PDE \(u_t=6uu_x-u_{xxx}\). Publication within 1974 is clear; precise issue-day priority relative to 23 September is not asserted.
fate: \citet[\S2]{novikov1974periodic}, received 18 February 1974 and published July 1974, proves stationary KdV implies finite-gap. The converse is explicit in \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}, received 3 June 1974 and published later in 1974. The full account is \citet[Chapter 2, \S2]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. Class A refers to that converse and full characterization, not to the already published forward implication. Earlier occurrences include 1973-326.15 and 1974-340.7.

title: Monodromy and its discriminant
notes: The normalized \(c,s\) solutions, the translation matrix \(\widehat T=(\alpha_{ij})\), \(\det\widehat T=1\), and \(\lambda^2-2\tau\lambda+1=0\) with \(2\tau=\alpha_{11}+\alpha_{22}\) are written.
statement: Normalize \(c(x_0)=s^{\prime}(x_0)=1\), \(c^{\prime}(x_0)=s(x_0)=0\). The period map on the two-dimensional solution space has determinant one by the constant Wronskian. Its eigenvalues are \(\tau(E)\pm\sqrt{\tau(E)^2-1}\); every matrix entry and \(\tau\) is entire in \(E\).
fate: Classical monodromy construction; \citet[Chapter 2, \S1, Eqs.~(2.1.1)--(2.1.8)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. Earlier occurrence: 1973-326.7.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Allowed and forbidden intervals from the discriminant
notes: An allowed energy has a Bloch function with \(|\lambda|=1\); \(\tau^2\le1\) is allowed and \(\tau^2>1\) forbidden. Two drawings correct the oscillation of the discriminant.
statement: For the real periodic problem, \(\sigma(L)=\{E\in\mathbb R:|\tau(E)|\le1\}\). Periodic and antiperiodic eigenvalues give band endpoints. Critical points of the discriminant above the spectral bottom lie in the closures of spectral gaps, and extrema alternate at levels at least1 and at most−1 respectively. A closed gap means a tangency at \(+1\) or \(-1\), not that the entire discriminant becomes constant.
fate: Classical Hill spectral theory; \citet[Chapter 2, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. The notebook\textquotesingle s later \(\max\) and \(\min\) both equal 1 is a sign omission, visible after the corrected sketch.

title: Closed gaps have scalar monodromy
notes: If \(\tau^2(E)=1\) has a multiple root, the notes infer \(\alpha_{12}=\alpha_{21}=0\), distinguishing a Jordan band edge from a diagonal one.
statement: For a real periodic Hill operator, a double periodic or antiperiodic eigenvalue has two independent periodic or antiperiodic solutions, so its monodromy is \(+I\) or \(-I\). Thus both off-diagonal entries vanish in every basis; a simple edge generally has a nontrivial Jordan block. This uses the differential equation and self-adjoint boundary problem, not the characteristic polynomial of an arbitrary matrix alone.
fate: Classical closed-gap criterion; \citet[Chapter 2, \S1]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}; earlier 1973-326.12.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Removing double branch points from the spectral curve
notes: There are \(2N+1\) simple finite roots \(E_j\) of \(\tau^2-1\), the other roots are double; a radical involving \((\tau^2-1)/\prod(E-E_j)\) is called single-valued.
statement: If the real periodic spectrum has exactly \(N\) open bounded gaps and distinct endpoints \(E_1<\cdots<E_{2N+1}\), then \((\tau^2(E)-1)/\prod_j(E-E_j)\) is entire with only even-order zeros, hence has an entire square root. The remaining two-sheeted compact curve is \(w^2=\prod_j(E-E_j)\), of genus \(N\).
reconstruction: The quotient under one square root is the mathematical reading, not a claim that the scan is unambiguous.
fate: The finite-gap reduction is in \citet[Chapter 2, \S\S1--2]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. The radical must include the quotient; the handwritten overbar alone does not decide its full scope. The spectral-curve and divisor statements are explicitly announced in \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}, received 3 June 1974 and published later in 1974; this is a firmer contemporary match than the later survey alone.

title: The Riccati logarithmic derivative
notes: \(\chi=-i\Psi^{\prime}/\Psi\); it is independent of the normalizing point \(x_0\), periodic in \(x\), and satisfies \(-i\chi^{\prime}+\chi^2+u-E=0\).
statement: For a chosen nonzero Bloch solution, away from its zeros, the logarithmic derivative is independent of scalar normalization, is \(T\)-periodic, and obeys that Riccati equation. Branch choice in spectral parameter remains; independence of \(x_0\) means that the same Bloch line is selected.
fate: Classical Riccati substitution, written in precisely this convention in \citet[Chapter 2, \S1, Eqs.~(2.1.10)--(2.1.12)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}.

title: Amplitude and phase of a Bloch solution
notes: \(\chi_I=\chi_R^{\prime}/(2\chi_R)\), \(\Psi=\sqrt{\chi_R(x_0,E)/\chi_R(x,E)}\exp(i\int_{x_0}^x\chi_R)\), and \(|\Psi|^2=\chi_R(x_0,E)/\chi_R(x,E)\) in an allowed band.
statement: For real \(u,E\) with \(E\) inside an open spectral band, choose a nonreal Bloch line and its conjugate, with nonzero Wronskian. Then \(a=\operatorname{Re}\chi\) never vanishes, \(\operatorname{Im}\chi=a^{\prime}/(2a)\), and the displayed normalized amplitude-phase formula holds with a continuous square root equal to 1 at \(x=x_0\). It need not hold at a band endpoint without a limiting interpretation.
fate: \citet[Chapter 2, \S1, Eqs.~(2.1.12)--(2.1.14)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} gives these formulas.

title: Formal high-energy densities and parity
notes: For \(E=k^2\), \(\chi\sim k+\sum_{n\ge1}\chi_n/(2k)^n\); the coefficients are differential polynomials in \(u\). The real part contains only odd inverse powers.
statement: For smooth real \(u\), the formal Riccati solution with leading term \(k\) is obtained recursively. In this convention \(\chi_1=-u\), \(\chi_2=-iu^{\prime}\), \(\chi_3=u^{\prime\prime}-u^2\). Odd coefficients are real and even coefficients imaginary; even terms are total derivatives and integrate to zero over a period. A formal expansion is not a claim of convergence.

fate: \citet[Chapter 1, \S1 and Chapter 2, Eq.~(2.1.18)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}; compare 1973-326.19.

title: Quasimomentum as a generating function
notes: \(\lambda=e^{ip(E)}\), \(p(E)=\int_{x_0}^{x_0+T}\chi_R(x,E)\,dx+2\pi n\); the Euler equations for its expansion are called KdV equations.
statement: For a selected Bloch branch, \(p\) is defined modulo \(2\pi\). Its high-energy expansion yields integrals of local differential polynomials invariant under isospectral KdV flows. Hamiltonian evolution generated by these integrals gives the KdV hierarchy; critical points of finite linear combinations give stationary equations. The Euler--Lagrange equation alone is not the evolutionary KdV equation.
reconstruction: The distinction between variational critical-point equations and Hamiltonian time evolution repairs an abbreviated phrase.
fate: \citet[Chapter 2, Eq.~(2.1.15) and \S2]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. The stationary hierarchy mechanism is already in \citet[\S2]{novikov1974periodic}. The cited Novikov article appeared inJuly 1974, before the23 September catalogue date; this occurrence is therefore expository.

title: Variational derivative of quasimomentum
notes: \(\delta p(E)/\delta u(x)=-1/(2\chi_R(x,E))\).
statement: For real smooth periodic \(u\), a spectral parameter in a band interior, and a fixed local branch of quasimomentum, its first variation under periodic \(v\) is \(D p(u)[v]=-\tfrac12\int_0^T v(x)/\chi_R(x,E)\,dx\). The local choice removes the additive \(2\pi\) ambiguity; analytic continuation requires consistent sheet choice.
fate: \citet[Chapter 2, Eq.~(2.1.17)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} gives the negative-sign formula. With the present convention \(p(E;u_0)=T\sqrt{E-u_0}\) for constant potential, direct differentiation gives \(\delta p/\delta u(x)=-1/(2\sqrt{E-u_0})\), so the negative sign is forced. The notebook agrees with this check.

title: Expressing the logarithmic derivative through monodromy
notes: \(\chi=\sqrt{1-\tau^2}/\alpha_{21}+\tfrac i2(\alpha_{11}-\alpha_{22})/\alpha_{21}\).
statement: Use the coefficient-basis convention \(T=\begin{pmatrix}c(T)&c^{\prime}(T)\\s(T)&s^{\prime}(T)\end{pmatrix}\), so \(\alpha_{21}=s(T)\). Solving the Bloch eigenvector equation gives the displayed expression, with the sign of the square root selecting the multiplier. Where \(s(T)=0\), interpret it meromorphically or use the other chart.

fate: The two basis conventions are distinguished in \citet[Chapter 2, Eq.~(2.1.19)]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear}. Changing to the usual fundamental-state matrix interchanges the off-diagonal indices.

title: The finite-gap polynomial divisor representation
notes: \(R(E)=\prod_{j=1}^{2N+1}(E-E_j)\), \(P(E,x)=\prod_{j=1}^{N}(E-\gamma_j(x))\), \(\chi=\sqrt R/P-\tfrac i2P_x/P\).
statement: For a nonsingular real finite-gap Schr\"odinger potential with \(N\) open gaps, choose the branch of \(\sqrt R\) behaving as \(E^{N+1/2}\), and the monic degree-\(N\) divisor polynomial \(P\). Then the logarithmic derivative has the displayed meromorphic expression on \(w^2=R(E)\). Its zeros and poles must satisfy the Schr\"odinger compatibility identity, so an arbitrary pair of polynomials does not suffice.

title: Bloch function on the hyperelliptic curve
notes: Dubrovin states that \(\Psi(x,x_0,E)\) is single-valued on \(\Gamma_N\), meromorphic away from infinity, with \(N\) zeros above \(\gamma_i(x)\) and \(N\) poles above \(\gamma_i(x_0)\).
statement: For nonsingular finite-gap spectral data with a nonspecial divisor of degree \(N\), the normalized Baker--Akhiezer function is single-valued and meromorphic on the curve minus its point at infinity; its polar divisor is bounded by the initial divisor and its zero divisor by the moving divisor, with \(N\) points counting multiplicity before cancellation. At \(x=x_0\) the function is 1, so coincident zero and pole divisors cancel. At infinity it has the prescribed exponential singularity.
reconstruction: Multiplicity, divisor cancellation, nonspeciality and the exponential behavior at infinity are made explicit; the literal count fails at the normalization point.
fate: \citet[Chapter 2, \S1, p.~77 and \S3]{dubrovinmatveevnovikov1976nonlinear} supplies the divisor description and theta-function inverse construction. The notebook proves circulation by 23 September 1974; the relevant announcements appeared 1974--1975. The spectral-curve and divisor statements are explicitly announced in \citet[\S3]{dubrovinnovikov1974periodicity}, received 3 June 1974 and published later in 1974; this is a firmer contemporary match than the later survey alone.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Unordered configurations and the electric-field map
notes: \(C_k(\mathbb R^n)\) consists of unordered subsets of cardinality \(k\). Unit charges define \(f_S\), with each particle sent to infinity and infinity sent to zero, and the resulting sphere map has degree \(k\).
statement: For \(n>1\), choose a decaying radial field with a pole of fixed local degree at each point of a configuration. Its one-point compactification gives a continuous map \(C_k(\mathbb R^n)\to\Omega^n_k S^n\), where the source sphere is based at infinity and the target at zero. Orient the target so that each positive pole contributes degree \(+1\); then the total degree is \(k\).
reconstruction: The based mapping space, n>1 for the electrostatic description, and orientation convention are made explicit. Scanning gives the corresponding construction also in dimension 1.
fate: The construction is already explicit in \citet[\S1, p.~213]{segal1973configuration}, published in 1973. Its description agrees unusually closely with the notebook.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

pages: P000569, homology display; P000570, stable limit
title: Stable homology approximation and group completion
notes: \(H_i(C_k(\mathbb R^n))\cong H_i(\mathrm{Map}_k(S^n,S^n))\) for \(i\ll k\). The right-hand side is homotopically independent of \(k\), while configurations stabilize by adding particles.

Adding a particle at infinity defines stabilization after choosing an end, and translation between components of the grouplike loop space identifies their homotopy types. This is a stable homology assertion, not a finite-\(k\) homotopy equivalence.
fate: \citet[\S1 and main theorem]{segal1973configuration} proves the group-completion formulation and states this consequence. The notebook gives no numerical stable range, so none is attributed to the 1974 lecture.

title: Configuration spaces as classifying spaces
notes: Fuchs says that \(C_k(\mathbb R^n)\) gives different classifying spaces, without naming the groups or a limiting dimension.
statement: Two standard instances make the remark precise: \(C_k(\mathbb R^2)\) is a classifying space for the braid group, and \(C_k(\mathbb R^\infty)\) is a classifying space for \(\Sigma_k\). For a fixed finite \(n\ge3\), the ordered configuration space is not generally contractible, so the unordered space cannot simply be identified with \(B\Sigma_k\).
reconstruction: The two examples are editorial explanations of a general remark, not transcribed assertions.
fate: The braid and stable symmetric-group interpretations form the background of \citet[\S1]{segal1973configuration}; the notebook itself specifies neither example. The statement is therefore an identified but only partially matched expository remark.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: The topology of signed configurations
notes: Finite subsets carry charges of either sign; opposite charges disappear when they meet. Components are indexed by the total charge \(k\in\mathbb Z\).
statement: Let \(C(M)=\coprod_{r\ge0}C_r(M)\). Form \(C^{\pm}(M)\) from \(C(M)\times C(M)\) by cancelling a point common to the positive and negative configurations, with the quotient topology. Particles of the same sign remain distinct. For connected Euclidean space, the invariant \(\#S_+-\#S_-\) labels the path components.
fate: This is McDuff\textquotesingle s positive-and-negative-particle functor, published in 1975: \citet{mcduff1975configuration}. The precise quotient is also given in \citet[\S1; Example 11.5]{kallel1998particles}. The notebook records its seminar circulation by 30 September 1974.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: The correct loop-space target for cancelling particles
notes: A tentative \(C_k^{\pm}(\mathbb R^n)\simeq\mathrm{Map}_k(S^n,S^n)\) is labelled \ru{гипотеза}; it is immediately followed by a target \(Y_n\) of dimension \(2n\).

title: Scanning a manifold into a section space
notes: \(C_k(M)\to\Gamma_k^{\mathrm{cpt}}(T_M^{\mathrm{comp}})\), with infinity added to each tangent fibre. A finite-range electric field is said to make the construction rigorous.
statement: For a smooth \(n\)-manifold, choose a Riemannian metric and sufficiently small scanning balls. A configuration determines a compactly supported section of the fibrewise one-point compactification \(\dot TM\); outside the scanning support it is the infinity section. The component of the section space is the one containing scanned \(k\)-particle configurations. Local charts are glued through the tangent-bundle transition maps.
fate: This is the scanning construction of \citet{mcduff1975configuration}; the bundle and relative-section formulation are made explicit in \citet[Theorem 1.1]{kallel1998particles}. Its status in the notebook is an announcement of McDuff\textquotesingle s result, published the following year.

title: Stable homology of configurations on manifolds
notes: The manifold scanning map is said to induce a homology isomorphism for \(i\ll k\), without specifying compactness, boundary conditions or a stable range.
statement: For a connected smooth open manifold of dimension at least2 that is the interior of a compact manifold with nonempty boundary, choose an end for stabilization. In each fixed degree, scanning from \(C_k(M)\) to the corresponding compactly supported section component induces an integral-homology isomorphism for all sufficiently large \(k\). The stabilized space and section space are homology equivalent. Closed-manifold and relative variants require their own formulation.
reconstruction: The stated finite-type open-manifold scope is a safe precise reconstruction. The notebook says only manifold; no assertion for arbitrary spaces or boundary conventions is inferred.
fate: The stable scanning theorem originates in \citet{mcduff1975configuration}; \citet[Theorem 1.1]{kallel1998particles} proves a broader particle-space formulation. The restricted open-manifold statement is sufficient to make the unqualified notebook sentence rigorous.

pages: P000570, failed restriction and boundary quotient
title: Particles disappearing at a boundary
notes: The map \(C(M)\to C(U)\times C(V)\) by restriction is marked discontinuous. For manifolds with boundary, \(\overline C(U)\) identifies configurations agreeing on the interior, so boundary particles disappear.
statement: Cardinality changes when a particle crosses the edge of an open piece, preventing continuity into the disjoint-union configuration topology. The relative space \(C(U,\partial U)\), formed by deleting particles on \(\partial U\), gives the required continuity at the exit locus. Collar choices provide compatible restriction maps for the gluing argument.
fate: The relative configuration construction is part of McDuff\textquotesingle s scanning proof; see \citet{mcduff1975configuration} and the explicit relative particle construction in \citet[\S6]{kallel1998particles}.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

pages: P000570, boundary theorem and disk proof
title: Relative configurations and the local disk calculation
notes: For \(U\) with nonempty boundary, \(\overline C(U)\simeq\Gamma(\dot TU)\). For a disk, radially pushing points to the boundary leaves at most one particle, and both sides become \(S^n\).
statement: In the relative scanning model for a compact connected smooth manifold with nonempty boundary, particles are allowed to disappear on all of the boundary and the target consists of sections with unrestricted boundary values. The local model is \(C(D^n,\partial D^n)\simeq D^n/\partial D^n\cong S^n\), while \(\Gamma(\dot TD^n)\simeq\mathrm{Map}(D^n,S^n)\simeq S^n\). For disconnected manifolds each component must meet the exit boundary.
reconstruction: Connectedness, the exit boundary, and unrestricted section values at that boundary are supplied to distinguish this statement from compactly supported scanning on the interior.
fate: The disk calculation follows from \citet[Proposition9.1 and Lemma 11.1]{kallel1998particles}. The notebook attributes the general relative theorem to McDuff; \citet{mcduff1975configuration} was verified bibliographically, but its full text was inaccessible in this run. The exact all-boundary generalization is therefore reported with a partial match, rather than claimed checked from that original paper. Boundary values fixed to infinity would produce a different target.
present_status: As of November 2026, this is an established result in the stated scope; the qualification in the statement is essential.

title: Boundary independence of the pressure

statement: For translation-invariant bounded finite-range interactions on compact lattice variables, with normalized product a priori measure, pressure exists along van Hove boxes and is unchanged by boundary conditions whose change affects only a boundary layer of bounded energy per interaction. title: Nonanalyticity in the infinite-volume limit

title: Area and perimeter laws require a specified model

title: Milnor number as local gradient multiplicity
notes: For an analytic germ without constant or linear terms, \(\mu(f)\) is the multiplicity of the zero solution of \(\partial f/\partial z_i=0\), also described as the maximum number of solutions to \(\partial f/\partial z_i=\varepsilon_i\) for small \(\varepsilon\).

title: Euler--Jacobi vanishing of the total residue
notes: For two degree-\(n\) polynomials \(P_n,Q_n\), the notes give \(\sum_{P_n=Q_n=0} R_{n-4}(x,y)/\det\bigl(\partial(P_n,Q_n)/\partial(x,y)\bigr)=0\), summing over all \(n^2\) zeros.

title: Gauge potentials as local connection forms

title: Finite evaluation representations and tensor products
notes: Gelfand replaces the interval by two points and lets \(g(x_1),g(x_2)\) act separately in \(H_1\otimes H_2\).
statement: At distinct points \(x_1,\ldots,x_r\), choose irreducible unitary representations \(\pi_j\) of \(SL_2(\mathbb R)\). The formula \(\pi(g)=\bigotimes_j\pi_j(g(x_j))\) defines an irreducible unitary current-group representation. Evaluation onto the finite product is surjective because this Lie group is connected and the interval permits interpolation. Conversely, irreducible representations of the finite product decompose as outer tensor products because \(SL_2(\mathbb R)\) is type I.
reconstruction: Distinct evaluation points, irreducibility and the distinction between an outer tensor product and restriction to the diagonal subgroup are supplied.
fate: The finite-product representation statement appears explicitly in \citet[\S1.3, Eq.~(14)]{vershikgelfandgraev1973functions}. It is background for the continuous tensor product, and recurs from 1969-180.4.

title: Characters and distributions, with the circle-valued qualification
notes: For \(g(x)=e^{i\alpha(x)}\), an irreducible representation is written \(e^{i\ell(\alpha)}\), with \(\ell\) a linear functional; smooth test functions give distributions.
statement: For the additive group of real smooth functions, continuous unitary characters are \(\alpha\mapsto e^{i\ell(\alpha)}\), with \(\ell\) a real continuous linear functional. Such functionals are distributions. To descend this formula to \(C^\infty([0,1],S^1)\), require \(\ell(1)\in\mathbb Z\), since two smooth lifts differ by a constant integral multiple of \(2\pi\). For continuous test functions the appropriate continuous dual consists of signed measures, rather than arbitrary distributions.
reconstruction: The distinction between the additive group and its circle-valued quotient, and the dependence on the test-function topology, are editorial qualifications.
fate: \citet[Introduction, pp.~87--88]{vershikgelfandgraev1973functions} uses the additive real current group, for which the formula has no period obstruction. The notebook\textquotesingle s circle notation requires the extra integrality condition. Related earlier occurrence:1969-180.9.

title: A spatially uniform irreducible current-group representation
notes: Gelfand asks whether there is an irreducible representation \ru{которое всюду устроено одинаково}.
statement: For \(X=[0,1]\), \(G=PSL_2(\mathbb R)\), and a positive multiple \(m=\lambda\,dx\) of Lebesgue measure, construct a nontrivial irreducible strongly continuous representation of \(C(X,G)\) whose equivalence class is invariant under measure-preserving transformations of \(X\) that act on the chosen current group by pullback. In the continuous model these transformations may be taken to be measure-preserving homeomorphisms; the step-function construction accommodates the corresponding measurable formulation. Require also that the restriction to currents supported in any nonempty open subinterval is nontrivial. This full-support condition excludes finite sets of evaluation points and follows from the positive measure on every such interval in the construction.
reconstruction: Uniformity is interpreted through the measure-invariance property explicitly stated in the matching paper. This is an existence theorem for the specified group and topology, not a classification of all current-group representations. Full support is the explicit reconstruction of everywhere in the question; measure-preserving homeomorphisms of an interval alone would be too small a symmetry group to exclude evaluation examples.
fate: This existence question is answered by \citet[Theorems2.2, 3.3 and 3.4]{vershikgelfandgraev1973functions}, already published in 1973. The result is related to 1969-180.2 and GP-1969-02, but only the earlier title is available: neither identity of their hypotheses nor resolution of the broader earlier problem is asserted.
present_status: As of November 2026, solved in the stated PSL2(R), uniform-topology setting by the 1973 multiplicative-integral construction. The classifying problem GP-1969-01 and the broader interval-support question GP-1969-02 are not thereby declared solved.

title: The complementary series in the real-line model
notes: For \(0<\lambda<1\), \(\|f\|_\lambda^2=\iint |t-s|^{-\lambda}f(t)\overline{f(s)}\,dt\,ds\), and \(T_\lambda(g)f(t)=f((\alpha t+\gamma)/(\beta t+\delta))|\beta t+\delta|^{\lambda-2}\).
statement: Complete a suitable dense test-function space in the positive kernel norm. The displayed operators extend to irreducible unitary representations for \(0<\lambda<1\), and factor through \(PSL_2(\mathbb R)\). Positivity can be seen from the Fourier multiplier \(c_\lambda|\xi|^{\lambda-1}\), with \(c_\lambda>0\). The completed space can contain generalized functions and is not simply a pointwise class of ordinary functions with an absolutely convergent integral.

title: The trivial representation is an accumulation point
notes: Gelfand stresses the existence of infinite-dimensional representations close to 1; a second parameter is written \(\rho\approx1\), beside \(\rho=1\) labelled the identity representation.
statement: The spherical matrix coefficients of the complementary series tend to 1 as \(\lambda\downarrow0\), uniformly on compact subsets of the group, after normalizing the spherical vector. Thus the trivial representation is not isolated in the unitary dual. An endpoint pullback formula with exponent0 is not itself trivial on every function: the trivial representation is obtained through the appropriate invariant subspace or quotient.

title: Finite-dimensional symmetric-power representations
notes: The substitution \(f(x_1,x_2)\mapsto f(\alpha x_1+\beta x_2,\gamma x_1+\delta x_2)\) is applied to homogeneous polynomials of degree \(n\), with weight \(n\) said to approximate dimension.
statement: The space of homogeneous polynomials of degree \(n\ge0\) in two variables has basis \(x_1^n,x_1^{n-1}x_2,\ldots,x_2^n\), and dimension \(n+1\). Linear substitution, using inverse or right-action convention consistently, gives the symmetric-power representation of \(SL_2\). Over \(\mathbb C\) it is irreducible; for the real noncompact group and \(n>0\) it is not a finite-dimensional unitary representation with a positive invariant norm.
reconstruction: The exact dimension and the nonunitary character of the finite-dimensional nontrivial examples are supplied; weight and dimension are not identified as equal.
fate: This is the elementary algebraic comparison preceding the unitary construction. The notebook does not cite a distinct theorem. Its role is contrasted with the infinite-dimensional unitary representations in \citet[\S1.1]{vershikgelfandgraev1973functions}; the dimension \(n+1\) follows directly by counting the displayed monomial basis.

title: The endpoint invariant functional and its trivial quotient
notes: At \(\lambda=0\), the norm degenerates to \(|\int f(t)\,dt|^2\); the last display says that integration is invariant under the exponent−2 fractional-linear action.
statement: On a suitable test space the limiting form is \(B_0(f,h)=(\int f)\overline{(\int h)}\). Its kernel is the codimension-one invariant subspace of zero-integral functions. The quotient is the trivial one-dimensional representation, since change of variables gives \(\int T_0(g)f=\int f\). The zero-integral subspace obtains a different nondegenerate invariant form from the first derivative of the kernel at 0; it is not given a positive norm by the zero form itself.

title: Dyadic refinement of the step-current group
notes: The constant subgroup is \(G\), the two-half subgroup is \(G^2\), then \(G^4\), and so on, with representations on tensor products of \(H_{\lambda/2^n}\).
statement: For the dyadic partition \(\mathcal P_n\) of the interval and \(m=\lambda dx\), \(0<\lambda<1\), each cell has measure \(\lambda/2^n\). Diagonal duplication embeds \(G^{2^n}\) into \(G^{2^{n+1}}\). The associated outer tensor product acts in \(\mathcal H_n=\bigotimes_{j=1}^{2^n}H_{\lambda/2^n}\). Dyadic step functions approximate every continuous current uniformly, but an arbitrary step function is not itself a continuous current.
reconstruction: The measure scaling and diagonal embeddings are supplied; the inductive union is not identified set-theoretically with the continuous-current group.
fate: This is the dyadic specialization of the directed Borel-partition construction in \citet[\S2.1--2]{vershikgelfandgraev1973functions}. The distinction between the step group and the continuous group is explicit in that paper.

title: Multiplicity one under diagonal restriction
notes: The notes state \(H_{\lambda/2}\otimes H_{\lambda/2}=H_\lambda\oplus\text{rest}\), with \(H_\lambda\) occurring once.
statement: If \(a,b>0\) and \(a+b<1\), the restriction of \(T_a\otimes T_b\) from \(G\times G\) to the diagonal \(G\) contains \(T_{a+b}\) with multiplicity one. The remaining decomposition contains only principal continuous and discrete series. Consequently the required intertwining isometry is unique up to a scalar of absolute value1.

title: The isometric diagonal delta embedding
notes: The intertwiner is written \(f(t)\mapsto f(t)\delta(t-s)\), labelled a unitary embedding.
statement: For \(a,b>0\), \(a+b<1\), the distribution \(f(t)\delta(t-s)\) belongs to the completed kernel tensor space and defines an isometry \(H_{a+b}\hookrightarrow H_a\otimes H_b\). Pairing two such diagonal distributions multiplies the kernels to give \(|t-s|^{-(a+b)}\). This is an isometric injection, not a surjective unitary isomorphism and not a claim that delta is an ordinary \(L^2\) function.
fate: \citet[Lemmas1.7--1.8 and Theorems1.6--1.7]{vershikgelfandgraev1973functions} gives the precise distributional interpretation and coherent multiple embeddings. The explicit delta formula removes the otherwise arbitrary phase choice under refinement.

title: An irreducible continuous tensor-product representation
notes: The iterated tensor spaces are nested, their inductive limit is completed, and the step-function representation is said to extend to continuous functions.
statement: Use compatible isometric intertwiners satisfying composition under refinement, then complete \(\bigcup_n\mathcal H_n\). This produces a unitary step-current representation. Matrix-coefficient continuity in the uniform topology permits a unique strongly continuous extension to continuous currents. With the finite positive measure used here, the multiplicity-one construction yields irreducibility; irreducibility does not follow merely from the existence of an arbitrary inductive limit.

fate: \citet[Theorems2.1--2.2, Lemma 2.2 and Theorem 3.3]{vershikgelfandgraev1973functions} proves compatibility, independence of phase choices, irreducibility and extension. These are already 1973 results, not new 1974 announcements.

title: The centered logarithmic Hilbert space
notes: The exponential scalar product uses \(-\log|t_1-t_2|\). The following page writes \(\widetilde f(x,t)=f(x,t)-1/[\pi(1+x^2)]\), although \(\int f(x,t)\,dt=1\).
statement: Set \(\rho(t)=1/[\pi(1+t^2)]\) and \(h_x(t)=f(x,t)-\rho(t)\), so \(\int h_x=0\). On real zero-integral test functions define \(B(h,k)=-\iint\log|t-s|h(t)k(s)\,dt\,ds\). Its completion is a real Hilbert space; for complex functions insert conjugation in the second argument. The form arises by differentiating \(|t-s|^{-\lambda}\) at 0 after the constant term has vanished.

pages: P000582, formal combinations and exponential product
title: Formal coherent vectors rather than ordinary functions
notes: Finite formal linear combinations of the labels \(f(x,t)\) are introduced; the notes emphasize that the symbol labelled by zero need not be the zero vector.
statement: Let \(\mathcal K=L^2(X,m;H_0)\), where \(H_0\) is the centered logarithmic Hilbert space. For real \(h\in\mathcal K\), introduce a formal vector \(e(h)\) and define \(\langle e(h),e(k)\rangle=\exp\langle h,k\rangle_{\mathcal K}\). Extend sesquilinearly, quotient any null vectors and complete. The exponential kernel is positive by its tensor-power series. In particular \(e(0)\) has norm 1, although the label 0 is the zero vector of \(\mathcal K\).

fate: \citet[\S6.1, Lemma 6.2, and \S6.3]{vershikgelfandgraev1973functions} gives this construction and its logarithmic integral form. It also recurs from the exponential-Hilbert-space discussion indexed as 1969-180.6; no identity with every earlier model is assumed.

title: The scalar cocycle restoring unitarity
notes: The endpoint fractional-linear action is multiplied by an unspecified \(\lambda(g,f)\).
statement: In the real-label model put \(b_g=T_0(g)\rho-\rho\), \(A_gh=T_0(g)h\), and let \(Q\) be the inner product after integration over \(X\). Then an explicit normalized action is \[U_ge(h)=\exp\{-Q(A_gh,b_g)-\tfrac12Q(b_g,b_g)\}\,e(A_gh+b_g).\] The cocycle identity \(b_{g_1g_2}=b_{g_1}+A_{g_1}b_{g_2}\) makes this an ordinary unitary representation for the real model. Omitting the scalar generally fails to preserve the exponential kernel.
reconstruction: The explicit multiplier and the ordinary-versus-projective distinction are supplied from the matching construction; the notebook records only the unnamed scalar factor.
fate: \citet[\S6.1, Lemmas6.1--6.3; \S6.3 and Theorem 6.2]{vershikgelfandgraev1973functions} provides the multiplier and proves equivalence with the preceding irreducible construction. Complex holomorphic restrictions can instead produce projective representations; they are not what this unqualified real-line display specifies.
